scenes.title: Unpivot
scenes.narration: Unpivoting is the reverse of a pivot: it turns columns back into rows, reshaping wide data into long data.

scenes.title: What unpivoting does
bullets: Folds several columns into a single value column
Adds a label column naming which column each value came from
Transforms wide format into long, tidy format
scenes.narration: Unpivoting folds several columns down into a single value column. Alongside it you get a label column that records which original column each value came from. The overall effect is to transform wide format into the long, tidy format that many analytics and reporting tools prefer.

scenes.title: Unpivot with UNION ALL
scenes.code:
SELECT product, 'Q1' AS quarter, q1 AS amount FROM sales_wide
UNION ALL
SELECT product, 'Q2', q2 FROM sales_wide
UNION ALL
SELECT product, 'Q3', q3 FROM sales_wide
UNION ALL
SELECT product, 'Q4', q4 FROM sales_wide;
scenes.narration: The most portable way to unpivot is a UNION ALL. Each SELECT reads one of the quarterly columns and emits it as a row, hard-coding the quarter label and aliasing the value as amount. Stacking the four selects with UNION ALL turns one wide row per product into four long rows, one per quarter.

scenes.title: Ways to unpivot

left.title: UNION ALL
points: Scans the table once per column

right.title: UNPIVOT / LATERAL VALUES
points: UNPIVOT in SQL Server and Oracle

scenes.narration: The UNION ALL approach runs everywhere and is easy to follow, but it can read the table once per column. Dedicated tools are tidier: SQL Server and Oracle offer an UNPIVOT operator, while engines like PostgreSQL use a CROSS JOIN LATERAL over a VALUES list, and both do it in a single pass.

scenes.text: Unpivot when a downstream tool wants long, tidy data — one value per row with a label column identifying its source.
scenes.narration: Reach for unpivot when a downstream tool expects long, tidy data, with one value per row and a label column identifying where that value came from.
